newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lowest French wheat refund bid covers 25,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Lowest French wheat refund bid covers 25,000 T.

text.p: The lowest bid of 0.47 Ecus for European Union wheat export refunds through France on Thursday was for a volume of 25,000 tonnes, grain traders said.
The bid equates to a fob export price easily above $140 per tonne, and probably closer to $145 per tonne, they said.
Cereals office ONIC reported total bids between 0.47 Ecus and 15.87 Ecus for a volume of 338,000 tonnes.
Traders said that including the lowest bid at 0.47 Ecus, a cumulative volume of 105,000 tonnes was being sought for refunds up to and including one Ecu per tonne.
Cumulative bids up to two Ecus covered 130,000 tonnes.
Bids up to three Ecus were for 170,000 tonnes, bids up to four Ecus were for 210,000 tonnes and those up to five Ecus covered a cumulative volume of 238,000 tonnes.

Five Ecus, seen as one possible cut-off when results are announced later on Thursday, would pitch French wheat around the same as higher quality hard red winter in the U.S., currently close to $140 for September.
Soft red winter, against which French wheat is often sold at par or slightly higher, is worth closer to $127.

Traders said the European Commission, unwilling to start off what could be another big crop year with a negative signal to the market, was likely to grant some volumes at Thursday's first auction of the 1997/98 season.
One said the Commission would find it difficult to reject the most aggressive bids up to around three Ecus, despite signs the world market had recently hit bottom.
Keeping a lid on exports competely would be an extra risk since the tenders, usually held every seven days, were only scheduled every other week in July and August, he said.
Others projected refund awards up to four or five Ecus.
